text.p: - The leftist United List of Social Democrats together with the Nationalist Party and Green Alternative started collecting signatures in support of a referendum on whether to limit the amount of forest estates nationalised after World War Two that could be returned to their previous owners.
- Police are still searching for a robber who stole four million tolars ($26,058) in various currencies from an exchange office in Ljubljana.
- Slovenia's Chamber of Economy said a lack of appropriate transparent legislation is the main obstacle to direct foreign investment in the country.
- Spanish state secretary at the foreign ministry, Ramon de Miguel, urged Slovenia to bring its legislation into line with EU standards as soon as possible.
- Slovenia's largest petrol trading company Petrol will list its shares on the Ljubljana bourse. A date for the listing is still to be determined.
- Organisers of the ski-jumping World Cup final in Planica managed to prepare the event despite warm weather. Over 100,000 visitors are expected in Planica over the weekend.
- Slovenian president Milan Kucan met Vatutin Halil Bala, the new Albanian ambassador to Slovenia, on Wednesday.
- Petrol refinery Nafta Lendava said it managed to pare its 1996 losses by 297 million tolars to 798 million.
